# GitHub Evidence Checklist: Agentic Software Engineering System: URL Shortener

**Purpose**: Validate that requirements specify which repository history and evidence must be visible to reviewers, and in what form.
**Created**: 2026-10-15
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md) · [plan.md](../plan.md) · [ADRs](../../../docs/adr/README.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.
**Item tags**: `[Mandatory]` means the criterion derives from the constitution, an approved requirement, or an accepted ADR or ruling. `[Optional]` means it concerns an enhancement. `[Dnn]` refers to a detection from the checklist brief; the detection map is in [../gates/release-evidence-gates.md](../gates/release-evidence-gates.md). Post-implementation evidence checks are in that gates file, not here. Every item is unchecked, including `[Optional]` items, so `/speckit-implement` reports this file as incomplete until a reviewer marks it.

## Requirement Completeness

- [ ] CHK001 Is the repository hosting specified (GitHub per CST-009), and are branch policy and pull-request expectations stated or explicitly left open? [Completeness, Spec §CST-009 (CR-003); CON X] [Mandatory]
- [ ] CHK002 Is it specified which evidence artifacts are committed (docs/evidence/<scenario>/<run-id>/manifest.json) and which stay in the gitignored `var/`? [Clarity, Plan §13] [Mandatory]
- [ ] CHK003 Is it required that committed evidence comes only from real runs, with integrity recorded (audit head hash)? [Completeness, CON X; ADR-008] [D23] [Mandatory]
- [ ] CHK004 Is it specified that secrets, `var/` runtime data and the confidential assessment source are never committed, with a scan required before push? [Completeness, CON V; CON X; Spec §CST-004] [Mandatory]
- [ ] CHK005 Is the submission tag specified exactly (annotated tag `assessment-submission-v1.0`), including which commit it must mark? [Clarity, Spec §CST-009 (CR-003); Governance §6] [Mandatory]

## Requirement Clarity

- [ ] CHK006 Are commit requirements (small, coherent, intent-describing) specified together with how they are assessed? [Clarity, CON X] [Mandatory]
- [ ] CHK007 Are lifecycle approvals (Human Gates, CR records) required to be traceable to commits? [Traceability, CON X] [Mandatory]
- [ ] CHK008 Is the disclosure of AI assistance specified for commits, change sets and the README section "How AI assistance was used and governed"? [Clarity, Spec §CST-009 (CR-003), §FR-ORC-034; CON X] [Mandatory]
- [ ] CHK009 Is a commit convention specified that makes "specification and test before implementation" visible in history (for example test commits preceding implementation commits)? [Gap, CON I; CON IV] [D24] [Optional]
- [ ] CHK010 Is the required GitHub Actions CI specified with the checks it must run (at least the test suite) and the commit it must pass on? [Completeness, Spec §CST-009 (CR-003)] [Mandatory]

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation
- `/speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `/speckit-specify` and `/speckit-clarify`
- `[Gap]` = the requirement is missing; `[Ambiguity]` = the term or rule needs a definition; `[Conflict]` = two sources disagree; `[Assumption]` = relies on an unvalidated assumption
